events.name: Shut up & Write: Broken Arrow
events.description:
Shut Up & Write hosts free in-person and online writing events for writers all over the world. Our goal is to ensure that every writer, regardless of genre or skill level, has access to the community, accountability, and resources they need to be successful in their personal writing goals. Our events use our proven formula: a few minutes of introductions, an hour of focused writing, and a final check-in to share the hour's progress.

What to Expect
RSVP and please arrive 10–15 minutes early to get settled at an in-person event. Our host will lead introductions and then everyone will write for a quiet, focused period of time.

Afterward, we’ll have an optional time to chat and get to know each other. Members often talk about their successes and challenges as writers. Our events are a safe space for writers to work on their craft. No one will read or critique your writing.
For more information about our events, visit https://shutupwrite.com.

Being Late is Okay: Just show up and get settled, then check in with me after the session. (I’ll be the person with the Shut Up & Write sign.) If you are on time, please be willing to make room for any friendly latecomers.

What Should I Bring?
Whatever you need to be able to write!
Bring earbuds/earplugs if you want to block the cafe’s ambient music or the occasional conversation by other patrons.

events.name: First Friday Art Crawl (Downtown Tulsa)
events.description:
Voted one of the Best Public Entertainment Events in Tulsa! The First Friday Art Crawl was established in 2007 so we are marking our 18thconsecutive year of this monthly display. This year-round monthly event features all of the galleries, studios and museums as well as the part-time galleries in various shops opening their doors to show art. The Art Crawl is held on the first Friday of the month, open from 6–9 pm and sponsored by the Tulsa Arts District Business Association.

In line with its original purpose, local artists are given an opportunity to display and sell their work at the various member businesses. This event has grown from 50–100 people visiting 4–6 venues to an event that has drawn over 3,000 people every month and continues to attract new people to Downtown Tulsa.

Besides the mini-galleries being open, the established museums and galleries offer free or reduced admission and many shops stay open late. During any given Art Crawl, visitors can expect visual art, performances and maybe a few fireworks! Each venue offers something different and creative, a true hallmark of the Tulsa Arts District.

First Friday is a perfect date night starting with a cocktail, coffee or early dinner on one of the many patios. It can also be a leisurely browse of the art and a great late dinner or nightcap at the District’s unique restaurants or clubs. Families can find many options from kid-friendly gallery shows to live music in the park. For those who like to linger even later, stay for one of the clubs, bars or coffee shops – many of which offer live entertainment.

Visit the website to see specific events happening for each individual First Friday

events.name: (Homemade Push Cart Race) Rascals on Route 66
events.description:
Rascals on Route 66 is racing into downtown Sapulpa on July 4th as part of the Centennial Celebration of Historic Route 66! This is a non-profit event. This high-energy, Red Bull Soapbox– and Little Rascals–inspired event features build-your-own, push-powered race cars tearing down Route 66 on Dewey Street. 

Racing begins at 8:30 AM (check-in 7:00–7:50 AM) with divisions for ages 4–9, 10–15, 16+ straightaway, and 18+ obstacle course. Each category is limited to 26 signups (subject to change). Trophy's for each category including best looking Cart! 

We are talking Crazy, Over the top themes. Giant chicken, Ice cream truck, Minecraft, etc. Go Big or go Home! Spectators attend free, racer registration are $25 for pre-registered and $40 day-of (104-racer limit). 

Come celebrate Independence Day, the Centennial of Route 66, and Sapulpa’s brand-new road—plus shopping, dining, and all-day fun!

events.name: Folds of Honor FreedomFest Presented by QuikTrip
events.description:
Folds of Honor FreedomFest presented by QuikTrip is back for another evening of patriotic fun! Visible for miles around, an estimated 80,000 spectators can enjoy the view from Dream Keepers Park, River West Festival Park, and along the Arkansas River including Gathering Place this 4th of July.

Spectators can experience the full effect of this patriotic celebration by tuning into radio sponsor KRMG (740 AM & 102.3 FM) during the display to listen to the accompanying musical score. This is where Tulsa Fireworks happen! If you want to see Tulsa’s BEST fireworks show, you’ll want to join us at Folds Of Honor FreedomFest 2023. For those celebrating at home, turn to KTUL Tulsa’s News Channel 8 to watch live coverage of the Fireworks Grand Finale in the opening moments of the 10 p.m. newscast. The 2023 fireworks display will be staged from the 21st Street Bridge.
